verified.claim: Gas caveat: 'about 1.97M of 2M' and 'with 60k gas the call reverts' reproduce (the second only as a top-level call), and the advice works
verified.evidence: Scratch Foundry project outside the repo (copies of ProofOfCover.sol and Types.sol, same compiler settings, looping account whose cover() is while(true){}): isCovered with a 2,000,000 gas cap returns (false, ...) after 1,974,453 gas measured around the call (1,969,917 in a second harness; earlier verifier 1,972,937): 'about 1.97M of 2M' holds. On the REAL deployed contract via eth_call with a state-override looping account at 0x1111...1111 (read-only, no transaction): gas limits 2,000,000 down to 80,000 return not-covered; 60,000 fails with 'out of gas'; the threshold lies between 62,109 (fails) and 62,187 (works), so 'with 60k gas the call reverts' holds for a call that has 60k in total. It does NOT hold for a nested call with a 60k cap: in Foundry that returns not-covered, and the smallest cap that returns is about 34,250 (cold) / 34,500 (warm); the chain adds about 30k of intrinsic and L1 cost at top level (eth_estimateGas of a trivial call here is 30,158). A pool following the advice (try poc.isCovered{gas: cap} catch -> false) used 28,371 / 31,368 / 51,443 / 100,623 / 297,498 total gas for caps of 20k / 30k / 50k / 100k / 300k and read the hostile account as not covered, so the grief is bounded by the cap. eth_estimateGas on the real chain: 70,285 covered account, 32,880 EOA, 31,759,383 looping account (an estimateGas artifact of the 63/64 rule at the block gas limit). SECURITY.md (table row, section 5) and PROOF_OF_COVER.md carry the caveat and the advice.

verified.claim: claim-letters: the scripted label is decided per settle; a Replay settle outside every session is scripted; a Replay settle with no block time is retried, not lettered (current script, sha1 1f8bfbaf1a41..., edited 06:50:17 IST)
verified.evidence: scripts/claim-letters.ts: isScripted() calls scriptedSettleTxs() (reads gap-demo.json and gap-party.json) and replaySessions() (reads rhTestnet.json: sessions[], current startsAt/speed, attempts[]) on every call; a session now ends at start + window/speed and an aborted attempt at stoppedAt, with no grace after the end. Scratch harness: byte-identical copy of the script, ROOT in a scratch tree, real deployments/ untouched; 33 of 33 checks behave as designed: a tx added to gap-demo.json (settleTx key, upper-case hex) or gap-party.json (settle.tx, the keeper's format) after earlier calls flips the label at once, even inside a session; editing the sessions in rhTestnet.json between calls changes the label at once; no session recorded (today) -> any Replay settle is scripted; mid-session -> organic; session start-1 s -> scripted; session end (inclusive) -> organic, end+1 s -> scripted; a settle caused by the scripted FRIDAY step at end+3 s or end+20 s, and at gapAt+25 s of the Gap Party session, with its tx in no record -> scripted; the designed Monday-step settle at end+365 s -> scripted; between two sessions -> scripted; Live settle -> never scripted unless a record names it; Replay settle with no block time -> null (handle() returns 'failed', the main loop re-queues it next pass, --once reports it failed and writes nothing); a settle named in a record with no block time -> scripted; an unparseable gap file is ignored; a push tx under friday.pushes is not mistaken for a settle; speed 0 ignored; string numbers accepted; an attempt with no stoppedAt ignored. The keeper's record shape (settle.tx and summary.settleTx, as in deployments/gap-demo-fork.json) is matched, and the keeper starts the gap when replayPhase() turns 'ended' (now >= startsAt + window/speed), the same instant the session ends here. Documented trade-off in the code comment: an organic settle on the replay's own last prices in the seconds after the end is labelled scripted too (the safe direction, but a letter would then call a real move a staged test).

verified.claim: Gas wording in docs/PROOF_OF_COVER.md ('Gas is the exception') and docs/SECURITY.md section 5 matches my measurements, with two points to tighten (versions of 07:13:11 and 07:33:58 IST)
verified.evidence: About 1.97M of 2M: 1,974,453 gas around a 2,000,000-gas capped call in Foundry (1,969,917 in a second harness). A transaction that gave the call about 62,000 gas or less in total ran out of gas: measured as eth_call on the real deployed ProofOfCover with a state-override looping account (no transaction), the smallest gas limit that returns was between 62,109 and 62,187 at about 05:55 IST and 60,505 in three runs at 07:53-07:54 IST, so it holds as 'about' but moves with the chain's L1 cost component (60,000 failed both times). A cap of about 34,000 was enough: with a Prober contract injected by state override on the real node (a fresh call each time, so cold), the smallest cap at which the looping account returns 'not covered' is 34,163; 34,250 cold in Foundry. Two points to tighten, neither makes a number wrong: (1) a pool needs a cap above what a legitimately covered account costs: the smallest nested cap that returns covered is 40,713 for the two Live-market accounts and 46,739 for the two Replay-market accounts, and below that the call fails: a scan of caps from 2,000 to 60,000 in 100-gas steps (a fresh call each) found one clean transition per account (out of gas, then covered) and no cap at which a covered account was reported 'not covered', so a too-small cap fails closed, but copying 34,000 would make every covered account fail; say so and suggest a round figure such as 100,000. (2) At top level the same covered accounts needed 67,213 to 75,353 gas limit in my runs, which also drifted by about 2,000 between runs.

verified.evidence: 'About 1.97M of 2M': 1,974,453 gas around a 2,000,000-gas capped call in Foundry (1,969,917 in a second harness). 'A transaction with a total gas limit of about 60,000 or less ran out': on the real deployed contract as eth_call with a state-override looping account, 60,000 ran out in every session (the smallest limit that returns was 62,109-62,187 at about 05:55 IST, 60,505 at 07:53 and 63,406 at 08:09 IST; it moves with the L1 cost component, so 'about 60,000 or less' is a safe lower bound). 'A cap such as 100,000 with room to spare, and treat a failure as not covered': above both needs by more than 2x, and a hostile account's burn at a 100,000 cap was 100,623 in total. Both earlier points to tighten (the cap needed for a covered account; the drift of the top-level figure) are now in the text.

summary: FIRST PASS (superseded by recheckSummary below; kept for the record): The backtest is solid: it reproduces exactly from fresh mainnet data, an independent re-implementation matches every claim, sensitivity and the money arithmetic, and BACKTEST.md matches the JSON. ProofOfCover tests (14), coverage (100%), the deployed contract's answers for all 4 team-operated accounts, random and special addresses, and the deployment record all hold; the explorer verification is partial, as disclosed. The claim-letter worker is safe: dry-run writes nothing into deployments/letters, no letter is written without a model, and the validator rejects bad letters. Status is partial because of six issues: ROADMAP says a scripted gap claim was paid on-chain and a keeper settles claims, but there are 0 Settled events on testnet; PROOF_OF_COVER.md still says it is not deployed; the 'never reverts' claim ignores gas griefing (a hostile account burns ~99% of forwarded gas); the worker reads the scripted-gap files once at start so it can miss the label; the Slither numbers could not be reproduced here; and the '24-hour heartbeat' caveat is wrong over weekends (gaps up to 77.8 h). I fixed nothing, as instructed. Note for the main session: the builder reported that sourcing .env printed a fragment of a secret from line 8 in the deploy transcript; I did not open .env and cannot assess it.

fixed.claim: ProofOfCover 'can never revert for any address' (SECURITY.md table; PROOF_OF_COVER.md)
fixed.originalProblem: True for return data and memory, but not for gas. A hostile account whose cover() loops forever makes isCovered burn 1,972,937 of 2,000,000 forwarded gas (my scratch Foundry test); with 60k gas the call reverts out-of-gas. A pool or contract that calls isCovered with an attacker-chosen account can be gas-griefed. Not documented; docs should say 'does not revert when given enough gas' and advise a gas cap on the staticcall.
fixed.evidence: Fixed. SECURITY.md's table row now reads '...or revert on any account's return data. It can run out of gas on a hostile account; see section 5', section 5 has the gas bullet, and PROOF_OF_COVER.md has 'Gas is the exception' with the advice to call with a gas cap and treat a failure as not covered. Numbers reproduce (1,974,453 of 2,000,000; 60,000 fails as a top-level call, threshold 62.1k) and the advice works (verified[]). Precision note for the wording: the '60k reverts' figure is for a call that has 60k in total; a nested call with a 60k cap does not revert (it needs about 34k).

fixed.originalProblem: My first pass (script as of 05:41, sha1 fb654d02978b...) ended each replay session 300 s after its window (the Replay maxPriceAge) and called any Replay settle inside that span organic unless a gap record named its tx. The keeper's gap starts right after the window ends and pushes the scripted Friday prices at once, and its settler settles ANY account past its limit within about 15 s; the gap record names only the target's settle tx. So a settle caused by the Friday step (an account with a limit under about 8%) was written with scripted:false and the model was not told to say 'scripted gap'. Reproduced in the scratch harness at session end+20 s and at gapAt+25 s of the Gap Party session.

fixed.claim: claim-letters --dry-run never writes to deployments/letters (the script's header comment and its error message)
fixed.originalProblem: Not on a case-insensitive filesystem, which is the macOS default and this machine's APFS. realPath() resolves symlinks with fs.realpathSync, which keeps the case you typed, and the guard compares strings, so --out-dir deployments/Letters (or deployments/LETTERS/nested, or a symlink whose target is spelled deployments/LETTERS) is not refused. Reproduced in a scratch tree with a byte-identical copy of the script (sha1 ebf52e44e1b5...): with letters absent, --dry-run --fixture events.json --out-dir deployments/Letters created the folder and wrote 2 template files into what the site and the worker see as deployments/letters; with letters present the same, and a symlink to deployments/LETTERS did the same. I did not try it against the real folder, to keep deployments/letters absent. It holds on a case-sensitive filesystem (the Linux droplet). The template files carry dryRun true, so the site ignores them, but a file named after a settle tx makes the real worker skip that settle ('exists'). Fix, verified in a scratch copy only: use fs.realpathSync.native for the existing part of the path and compare the two paths lower-cased; that refused deployments/Letters, deployments/LETTERS/nested (letters absent and present) and the case-variant symlink while every other refusal and the safe control kept working. Writing templates into the deployments folder itself (--out-dir deployments, or a symlink to it) is also still allowed; it is not the letters folder but is worth refusing too.
fixed.evidence: Fixed at 08:06:46 IST: see the verified[] entry on the guard. Case variants (deployments/Letters, deployments/LETTERS/nested, a symlink whose target is spelled in another case), --out-dir deployments, a symlink to deployments and every other case are now refused or fail without writing, the controls still work, and deployments/letters stayed absent in the real repo.

claim-letters: an ancestor of deployments, such as --out-dir . (the repo root), is accepted by the dry-run guard and writes template files there. Not a letters risk.

The docs say 'a transaction'; I measured eth_call on the real contract (no transaction may be sent). On Arbitrum the L1 cost counts against a transaction's gas limit in the same way, and the limit that is needed moves with the L1 fee (60,505 to 63,406 in three hours), so 'about 60,000 or less ran out' stays true and is a lower bound, not a limit that is enough.
